repairVerification.finding: CODEX-V1-B1 — machineSurface did not define the stable machine/schema/version contract OBL-2 requires; it named only a family (SARIF 2.1.0 + property-bag roots)
howIChecked: machineSurface now declares projectionSchemaId 'opensip-sarif-projection.1' and projectionSchemaVersion 1, with two rooted property objects (run.properties.opensip, result.properties.opensip) and an explicit key/type/requiredness map at each: schemaId (string, fixed value), schemaVersion (integer, fixed value) and truncation (object, required ['truncated'], boolean truncated, optional string kind) requiredAlways on the run; artifactRefs (array of {ref:string}, mayBeEmpty, cardinality 0..n) requiredAlways on the result; verdict gated on requiredWhenHostVerdictExists; runId, findingId and coverage gated on requiredWhenDr006Active.

The requiredness rule is stated as a rule, not left to inference: requiredAlways keys MUST be present on every advertised emission, requiredWhen* keys MUST be present iff DR-006 is ACTIVE and MUST be omitted — explicitly 'not null' — while INACTIVE. Cardinality is stated separately (one run object per run, one result object per result).

Version behavior is closed in three directions: additive unknown keys under properties.opensip MUST be preserved in the serialized bytes even if a consumer UI hides them; same schemaId at a higher version is additive iff every requiredAlways/requiredWhen* key survives with the same type and meaning; removing, renaming or reinterpreting any of the seven named preserved fields requires a new projectionSchemaId and is a failed successor.

goldenShape gives OBL-2 a reviewable shape rather than prose: a typed input triple, an expected object, and a pass rule with three named failure modes (missing required key, extra additive key allowed, relocated identity fails).

I checked the anti-alias guard independently of the repair's own claim: forbiddenNativeIdentityAlias states run.automationDetails.guid and result.guid are NOT the OpenSIP Run/Finding identity, and goldenShape.pass restates guid-as-runId as a failure. This is what keeps the schema from minting an identity recipe by the back door while DR-006 is INACTIVE.

It is a consistency nit in the surface that CODEX-V1-B1 asked to be made exact, not a defect in what the surface says. Flagged only so a successor can normalize on one idiom.

All three claimed repairs of the frozen Codex v1 REJECT are real and verified at source: CODEX-V1-B1's missing machine contract is now a closed key/type/requiredness map under opensip-sarif-projection.1 with cardinality, version behavior, a structured goldenShape, and a guid-as-identity prohibition that keeps it from minting a DR-006 recipe by the back door; CODEX-V1-S1's standingless loss fixture now has previewStanding INACTIVE on the same DR-006 advertisement ride as FC-PARITY, with zero INACTIVE classes anywhere lacking a ride; CODEX-V1-S2's dropped boundary is restored as an explicit committed-Run condition and the ordinary/authority-injection conflation is split into FC-OUTFAIL and FC-NONAUTH. Every dispatch attack is refuted against live bytes rather than against the artifact's self-description: the file 08 pin reproduces and line 304 is byte-identical to rowVerbatim as the sole '| DR-122 |' line; the 26 carried file 01 lines match exactly; the D9 golden is cited from file 01 L92-99, not minted; the v1-to-v2 leaf-path diff yields zero paths outside the nine-entry closed roster, so the completeness sentence holds and /date did not drift; and preview SARIF and G17 stay dropped, confirmed in live COORD at D-086 and D-092. Three advisories travel and none blocks: a stale COORDINATOR-DECISIONS pin whose dependent claims I re-verified against live bytes, a load-bearing preview-honesty citation that resolves into an unpinned disposition artifact, and one mixed requiredness idiom in the truncation block.
